title: fix(app-shell,console): an admin override reads as one — before the click and in the timeline
body:
Fixes #5178

An admin holding **no slot** in a request's pending-approver slate saw the exact same filled **Approve** / **Reject** / **Reassign** a designated approver sees. One unmarked click takes the framework#3424 privileged branch, which is *authoritative* — it finalises the node even under `per_group` / `unanimous` / `quorum`, bypassing every co-sign group that has not voted. The real incident behind the card: a PM clicked Approve *"to see if it was real"* and finalised a stage for an approver who never acted.

**No fork.** The card's fork clause asked me to check whether the timeline's data door exposes `via_override`. It does, end to end, so both halves ship here:

- `plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` — `rowFromAction` projects `via_override` (its comment literally says "surfaced so a timeline can SAY 'overridden the approver slate'")
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts` — the contract declares it, with "Consumers render the distinction"
- `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` — `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id/actions` returns `res.json({ data: rows })` over exactly those rows

Nothing was filed back to `objectstack`.

## Premise re-measured on `origin/main` @ `a2a974779`

Confirmed, matching the card and the PM: `via_override` has **zero** hits repo-wide (reverse-checked against `can_override`, which resolves in 5 files, so the zero is real). `can_override` is read only to *show* buttons, never to mark them.

## What changed

**Affordance.** A viewer the server reports as `can_act: false` **and** `can_override: true` now gets a warning-styled action labelled as an override (`Override Approve`), with a shield icon and `data-override-decision`, replacing the declared `primary` / `danger` styling meant for the assigned approver. The dialog it opens **names the pending approvers being bypassed**.

**Timeline.** Override rows now carry an `Admin override` chip and an amber dot, in **both** timelines — the record page's approvals panel and the Approval Center. This is framework#4466's own *Expected* ("surfaced in the timeline"), the half that never landed.

## Two design points that are load-bearing

**1. The warning rides the param dialog, not a chained confirm.** These decision actions collect params, so the param dialog is already the confirm — nothing is POSTed until its own Confirm. Putting a `confirmText` in front of it produces a first prompt that already reads as "the action ran" (framework#7278, maintainer ruling 2026-08-10: *one condition, one wording, one dialog*). So the override framing rides that dialog's own title and description. The PM's route suggestion said "behind a confirm"; this is that confirm, in the shape the ruling requires.

**2. The notice travels as its own dispatch key, NOT folded into `description` — and this is a measured hazard, not a preference.** `paramCollectionHandler` resolves the description through `actionDescription(...)`, which **prefers a `_actions.*.description` bundle hit over the passed literal**. And `plugin-approvals` **ships** exactly such an entry for `approval_reject`, in en / zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES. A warning routed through `description` would have been silently replaced by the ordinary "Reject this request?" copy in every locale carrying the bundle — a translation deleting the safety copy on the one privileged path it guards, with nothing red to show for it. Reproduced under ablation; see below.

**Which actions get the treatment is read from each action's own declared `visible` gate** (does it OR in `can_override`?), not a hard-coded name list. So a future decision action still ships as metadata alone, and `approval_recall` — gated on `is_submitter` — is never relabelled, even for a submitter who also holds override rights.

## Permission boundary

Nothing is relaxed. Who may act or override is unchanged, the dispatched request is byte-identical (pinned by a test), and no audit record is altered — this renders one that was already being written, and adds friction in front of a privileged path.

## File surface — increment declared

My claim comment named `views/RecordDetailView.tsx`, `hooks/useRecordApprovals.ts`, `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx`, `approvalsApi.ts`. Measurement moved it. **`RecordDetailView.tsx` needed no edit at all** — it mounts `DeclaredActionsBar`, which is where both hosts' decision buttons actually render, so it is the single choke point for the affordance. Added, all inside `packages/app-shell/src/{views,hooks,utils}` and `packages/i18n`, none in the OUT list (`app-shell/src/console/**`, plugin-grid, plugin-kanban), and no open PR touches any of them:

- `views/DeclaredActionsBar.tsx` — the affordance
- `views/RecordApprovalsPanel.tsx` — the record page's timeline (the card's "timeline" half; the PM's list predated reading it)
- `hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` — the notice reaching the param dialog undefeatably
- `views/ActionParamDialog.tsx` — one class, `whitespace-pre-line`, so the two-paragraph description renders as authored
- `utils/approvalOverride.ts` (new, + tests) and the two barrels that export it
- `packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts` — 5 new keys in all ten packs

## i18n

Every new string goes through the existing `approvalsInbox.*` path (the namespace both timelines already share so they cannot drift), with real translations in all ten locale packs. No count-driven plural, so no `ru` / `ar` plural-category trap — the approver list interpolates as `{{who}}`, matching the neighbouring `whyDisabled` key.

## Verification — all at `0a2b41ba0`

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/ packages/app-shell/src/hooks/ packages/app-shell/src/utils/
  → 321 files, 3323 passed | 1 skipped     exit 0
pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/ packages/i18n/
  → 101 files, 1478 passed                 exit 0
pnpm --filter app-shell --filter console --filter i18n type-check   exit 0
pnpm --filter app-shell --filter console --filter i18n lint         exit 0 (200 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors)
check:control-bytes / i18n-keys / i18n-drift / self-import / action-forward-parity / phantom-deps   all exit 0
check-changeset-presence / check-changeset-no-major                 exit 0
```

`check:i18n-keys` reports the 5 added keys resolving with full interpolation parity; `check:i18n-drift` reports 0 en values changed (additions only).

### Reverse verification

Both legs run from the committed state, restored by `git checkout` against the branch. All four suites import the module under test by **relative source path**, so there is no `dist/` indirection for an ablation to hide behind.

- **Leg A** — revert the three implementation files to `origin/main`: **3 of 4 suites red, 11 tests red**. The fourth (`approvalOverride.test.ts`) stays green correctly: it pins the pure predicate module, which the ablation does not touch.
- **Leg B** — the sharper one. Replace the implementation with the *naive* version (fold the notice into `description` and let `actionDescription` resolve it): **exactly 1 of 5 tests red**, and it is the bundle-hazard test:

  ```
  AssertionError: expected 'Bitte bestätigen Sie die Ablehnung di…' to contain 'Qian Hua'
  ```

  The bundle value replaced the entire warning, approver names included. That test is a real detector, not a tautology.

- Restored: **41/41 green**, working tree byte-identical to `HEAD`.

## Note on the shipped predicate spelling

The component suite uses the reduced `record.viewer.can_act || record.viewer.can_override` spelling, as the sibling approval suites already do: the shipped predicates carry #8990 sparse-face `has(...)` guards that need the `@objectstack/formula` engine, and a bare string normalizes onto the legacy JS path where `has(...)` faults and the gate fails closed (every button vanishes and the suite asserts nothing). The reduction cannot hide drift — `actionAdmittedByOverride` is pinned against the **verbatim** shipped predicate, `has(...)` guards and all, in `utils/approvalOverride.test.ts`.

CI has not converged at the time of writing; per the dispatch contract the report lands at draft-PR time and gate convergence is the PM's read.
